sights.w: The oldest mosque in Hougang, built in 1921 on land donated by Gujarati merchant-philanthropist Ahmad Mohamed Salleh Angullia to serve the area's Muslim community of farmers and traders. A stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail, just off Upper Serangoon Road near Kovan.
sights.k: Active mosque; visitors welcome outside prayer times

sights.w: Completed in 1987 and designed by Tay Kheng Soon of Akitek Tenggara, this is widely regarded as Singapore's first truly modernist Chinese temple — its roof rising in eight-sided prisms that evoke a lotus, its corners deliberately kept un-sharp on the deities' guidance. A Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gem' and a documented modern-movement building.

sights.n: Church of St Vincent de Paul
sights.w: A Catholic parish on Kovan's western edge whose roots trace to 1959, when Fr Henri Saussard began ministering to the rubber tappers, fishermen and farmers of the Jalan Kayu area; the present church was blessed and opened at Christmas 1970. It continues to serve the north-eastern Catholic community around Serangoon Gardens and Kovan.
sights.k: Active parish; Mass times on the church site

sights.w: Kovan's neighbourhood mall, renamed Heartland Mall in 2001 from the former Emporium outlet and integrated with Kovan MRT station (opened 2003) beneath Upper Serangoon Road. The daily shopping-and-transit heart of Kovan.
sights.k: Mall hours daily; above Kovan MRT

sights.n: Sungei Serangoon Park Connector (North-Eastern Riverine Loop)
sights.address: Along Sungei Serangoon / Sungei Pinang, Hougang, Singapore
sights.w: A waterside link in the North-Eastern Riverine Loop, running from Punggol Park along Sungei Serangoon and Sungei Pinang towards Punggol Promenade. Bioswales, reservoir edges and wetlands make it a scenic, bird-rich stretch for evening strolls and cycling on the Hougang edge.
